starters.name: Monolith
starters.summary: One application, built and deployed as a unit
useWhen: A new product or a small team, where one deployable keeps change cheap.
Explaining where a request goes before any of it is split out.
watchOutFor: Every change ships the whole application.
Layers blur over time unless their boundaries are kept on purpose.

starters.name: Modular Monolith
starters.summary: One deployable, explicitly encapsulated modules inside
useWhen: You want clear ownership without the cost of distributed services.
Preparing a monolith to split later, one module at a time.
watchOutFor: Module boundaries only hold if calls go through the public interface.
A shared database makes it easy to reach into another module's tables.

starters.name: Microservices
starters.summary: Independently deployed services, each owning its data
useWhen: Teams need to deploy and scale parts of the system independently.
Mapping which service owns which data.
watchOutFor: Calls between services fail and are slow in ways in-process calls are not.
Queries that span services need their own design.

starters.name: Event-Driven
starters.summary: Pub/sub: a topic fanning out to per-subscriber queues
useWhen: Several consumers react to the same change without the producer knowing them.
Showing retries and where failed messages go.
watchOutFor: Delivery is at least once: consumers must handle duplicates.
The flow of one request is harder to follow end to end.

starters.name: Hexagonal
starters.summary: Adapters around a core that owns its ports
useWhen: Keeping business rules independent of frameworks, databases and transports.
Testing the core without infrastructure.
watchOutFor: More indirection than a small service may need.
Ports drift into thin wrappers if they mirror one adapter.

starters.name: Backend for Frontend
starters.summary: A backend per frontend, over shared capabilities
useWhen: Web and mobile need different shapes of the same data.
Frontend teams want to change their API without coordinating every release.
watchOutFor: Logic duplicated across BFFs instead of living in the shared services.
One more service per client to run.

starters.name: CQRS
starters.summary: Distinct command and query paths, async read projection
useWhen: Reads and writes have very different shapes or loads.
Explaining eventual consistency between the two sides.
watchOutFor: Reads lag behind writes.
Two models to keep in step as the domain changes.

starters.name: Medallion
starters.summary: Refine raw data into validated, business-ready datasets
useWhen: Building analytics on data from several operational sources.
Showing where data quality is enforced.
watchOutFor: Each layer stores another copy of the data.
Late-arriving or corrected data needs reprocessing through every layer.

starters.name: Kappa
starters.summary: Process live and historical data through one durable stream
useWhen: Real-time views where reprocessing history must use the same code.
Replacing a separate batch layer.
watchOutFor: Replays of a long log take time and capacity.
The log's retention decides how far back you can rebuild.

starters.name: Change Data Capture
starters.summary: Capture committed changes once, fan out to derived views
useWhen: Keeping other systems in sync with a database without dual writes.
Feeding search, caches or analytics from the source of truth.
watchOutFor: Derived views are eventually consistent.
Schema changes in the source ripple to every consumer.

starters.name: Saga – Orchestration
starters.summary: Local transactions and compensation, one coordinator
useWhen: A workflow spans several services and must undo completed steps on failure.
You want one place that knows the workflow's state.
watchOutFor: The orchestrator can become a bottleneck or a god service.
Every step needs a compensation that really undoes it.

starters.name: Saga – Choreography
starters.summary: Local transactions chained by events, with no coordinator
useWhen: Few steps, owned by different teams, that already communicate through events.
Avoiding a central workflow service.
watchOutFor: The whole workflow is visible only by following the events.
Cyclic dependencies between services creep in as steps grow.

starters.name: Transactional Outbox
starters.summary: Persist state and event intent atomically, publish after
useWhen: A state change and its event must never disagree.
Publishing events from a service that owns a database.
watchOutFor: Events arrive at least once and slightly late.
The outbox table needs cleaning up.

starters.name: Order processing
starters.summary: Follow an order from the API through a queue to storage
useWhen: Learning how shapes, connectors and flows read on the canvas.
A starting point for any queue-and-worker design.
watchOutFor: It is deliberately small: there is no failure path.
